A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ShaPO research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original safety-alignment experiments across four model backbones, including domain-shift and noisy-supervision results, geometry-control ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds neuron-ratio sensitivity, Hessian-curvature measurements, and reward-supervision ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the probe-selected safety subspace, Top-1% default, token-level and reward-level objectives, and SAM-style updates. The new experiments analyze existing components without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on PKU-SafeRLHF-30K and evaluate the same five safety benchmarks, including the same domain-shift and preference-label-flipping scenarios. The added diagnostics use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 5 adds evaluated DPO+Reward and Dr.DPO+Reward controls against the corresponding ShaPO-R instantiations. Comparator membership in the original benchmark experiments is unchanged; newly cited methods in Appendix B are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a selected-neuron-ratio sweep from 0.01% to 100%, maximum Hessian eigenvalue measurement, and reward-supervision controls on LLaMA-3-8B. These are additional diagnostic protocols; the original benchmark settings, judges, backbones, and documented training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 substantially expands mechanistic validation beyond the existing geometry-control and composability comparisons. New Figure 5 tests sensitivity to subspace size, Table 4 connects curvature with alignment performance, and Table 5 separates reward-supervision benefits from additional geometry-control benefits.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added diagnostics continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive findings about neuron-ratio sensitivity, curvature, and reward-controlled gains. Figure 5 reports minimum OOD ASR at Top-1%; Table 4 reports Max HE of 25.2336 for Base and 6.2466 for ShaPO-T. In Table 5, DPO+Reward has OOD MD/NV ASR of 17.33%/7.02%, versus 15.98%/6.26% for DPO-based ShaPO-R. These are newly reported comparisons, not revisions to the unchanged results in Tables 1–3 and the existing appendices.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, robustness approximations, and Appendix C assumptions and derivations are unchanged. V2's Hessian table adds empirical measurements rather than new mathematical definitions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: selective geometry control, token-level and reward-level instantiations, robustness under domain shift and noisy supervision, and composability with data-centric methods. The new analyses support these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the neuron-ratio optimum as balancing safety-relevant coverage against redundant constraints, associates lower curvature with stronger alignment, and argues that geometry provides gains beyond reward supervision. The existing limitations concerning computational overhead and approximate subspace identification remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract. Algorithm details, probe implementation, hyperparameters, hardware, batch sizes, and reported running times in the appendices are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds references to winsorized DPO, BalDRO, sharpness-aware poisoning, and two CLIP robustness/subspace works while retaining the original data-centric versus geometry-centric positioning. Consolidating duplicate Bai references and updating Xu et al.'s publication metadata do not change the underlying cited works.

P1.justification: V2 locally rewrites and expands Section 4.5, adds acknowledgements, and updates author affiliations, contribution notes, and publication information. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain stable. Section 4.4 introduces an incorrect reference to Figure 5 instead of the retained noise-results Figure 3.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-panel neuron-ratio Figure 5 and Tables 4–5, with accompanying page reflow. Existing appendix figures and tables are retained and renumbered; the earlier displays undergo no substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: The neuron-ratio test, curvature measurements, and especially the reward-only controls strengthen empirical support for the retained method and address questions left open in v1. The code-access information also helps reproducibility. These gains remain limited to single-backbone diagnostics without uncertainty estimates; Table 5 supports complementary reward and geometry benefits more clearly than its strongest causal wording suggests, and the new noise-figure cross-reference is incorrect.
